title: Common Idiomatic Structures
summary: Learn high-frequency Brazilian structures such as dar para, acabar de, deixar de, levar jeito, and ter a ver.

sections.heading: Dar para and dá para
sections.body: **Dar para + infinitive** expresses possibility or feasibility. It is very common and often softer than poder.

examples.en: Is it possible to go on foot?
It wasn't possible to finish today.
Do you think it would be possible to reschedule?

sections.heading: Aspectual idioms
sections.body: Structures like **acabar de**, **deixar de**, **voltar a**, and **passar a** describe stages of an action: just did, stop doing, resume, start doing as a new pattern.

examples.pt: A empresa passou a aceitar Pix.

sections.heading: Evaluation and relation
sections.body: Idioms such as **ter a ver**, **não ter nada a ver**, **levar jeito para**, and **fazer questão de** are central to natural Brazilian expression.

examples.pt: Isso tem a ver com o trabalho.
examples.en: This has to do with work.
He has a knack for cooking.

keyPoints: Dá para is a flexible way to ask about possibility.
Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done'.
Passar a + infinitive means to begin doing as a new practice.
Ter a ver means 'to have to do with', not literal seeing.

commonMistakes.wrong: Isso tem que ver com você?
commonMistakes.right: Isso tem a ver com você?
commonMistakes.note: The common structure is ter a ver.
After dá para, use the infinitive.
